subject: Scaling pathway and staged commit uplift — fallback rate guardrails
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@acmeai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Scaling pathway and staged commit uplift

Hi Kimberly —

We’ve been watching steady growth on our chat assist feature and expect to double token volume in Q1. Before we lock in a longer-term commit, I wanted to understand: if we push a higher hosted monthly commit with Redwood, can we do a staged uplift over 3 months (50% -> 80% -> 100%) and have a clear fallback if we hit rate limits or capacity constraints?

Two specific asks:
- A proposal for a staged commit schedule with month-over-month pricing and any pro-rated credits.
- A fallback routing policy (e.g., model variant fallback, burst window behavior) so our fix-rate SLAs don’t degrade for customers.

I can share our usage extract but wanted to align on terms first.

Thanks,
Carlos Ruiz
Head of Platform
Acme AI

Attachment: acme-usage-extract.csv (1.2MB, CSV)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@acmeai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scaling pathway and staged commit uplift

Carlos —

Thanks for the heads up and for sharing the usage extract. We can absolutely support a staged commit uplift and provide explicit fallback behavior so your customer-facing latency and error budget remains intact. High-level proposal:

1) Staged commit schedule: 3-month ramp with pro-rated billing on each step (50% -> 80% -> 100%). Final price locks at month 4.

2) Fallback policy: automatic routing to a smaller quantized model variant when the hosted cluster signals >90% queue depth; plus a temporary increase in burst capacity for critical routes (up to 2x for 10 minutes) while we failover requests.

3) Rate guardrails: we’ll set per-route rate limits tied to the commit band; if you exceed the band we’ll throttle to a soft cap and surface a realtime alert.

I’m looping in Lauren to provide the pricing quote and Marcus to outline the staged rollout steps from the infra side. Can we do a 30-min call Monday to finalize?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scaling pathway and staged commit uplift — quote attached

Carlos —

Appreciate the context. Attached is a preliminary quote (redwood-quote-v3.pdf) and a staged-commit-plan.xlsx that maps the monthly commit bands to per-token rates and burst window behavior. Highlights:

- Month 1 (50% uplift): 30% discount on incremental tokens above current baseline; soft burst window of 15 minutes at 1.75x baseline throughput.
- Month 2 (80% uplift): 35% discount on incremental tokens; burst window 30 minutes at 1.5x baseline throughput.
- Month 3 (100% uplift): Final committed rate with a 40% discount on incremental tokens and standard burst policy.

We’ll include a fallback SLA clause: when queue depth >90% or 95th p50 latency degrades >300ms we automatically enable model-variant fallback (smaller quantized variant) for non-critical routes and apply a documented crediting approach if customer-visible errors occur.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm the ramp percentages and effective start date.
2) Legal to review the fallback SLA wording (we’ll prepare a short amendment).
3) Sign the DocuSign for the quoted commit and we’ll schedule a technical handoff.

I’ve also added the HubSpot deal id to the quote. Let me know availability for Monday 11/24 or Tuesday 11/25 for a 30-min finalize call.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-quote-v3.pdf, staged-commit-plan.xlsx

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scaling pathway and staged commit uplift — rollout & fallback details

Carlos / team —

Quick tech note from infra: the staged uplift you described is straightforward operationally, with a couple of recommendations to minimize customer risk:

- Canary rollout by route: increase commit allocation for low-risk routes first (internal flows, non-critical API endpoints) then expand to customer-facing routes after 48–72h of stable telemetry.
- KV/prefix caching warmup: we recommend a 24–48h preheat window for hot prefixes before each jump to avoid cache-miss storms.
- Fallback behavior: when we trigger the quantized-model fallback, we’ll also apply context-aware sampling so long-form generations use the full model while short chat responses can use the quantized path. This minimizes perceptible regression.
- Observability: we’ll provide a per-route dashboard and a webhook for your ops team with alerts when we enter fallback.

Rishi — looping you for any billing/commit accounting caveats.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
